notes.text:
This is a registration of existing caller premises, not a new equation theorem. The retained domain is a complete real-valued non-Archimedean K of characteristic and residue characteristic zero; X/K smooth, geometrically integral and projective, n>=2; L an actual ample rational line bundle; T=X^an; raw V=(L^n)>0. Exactly O217,D214,N220,T171,Q222,C218,G227,M257,S269 and all their clarifications are authorized. All 26 immutable mathematical bodies, including parallel arguments/clarifications, were read in bounded native file output. All 26 and the 62 separately authorized original primary byte/hash bindings match. Whole-body reading and hash checks are separate acts.

The exact mathematical premises used subsequently are these. O defines actual psh as decreasing weighted algebraic FS-net endpoints on the same rational bundle, excluding identically -infinity; energy is the infimum of continuous psh majorant energies. E1 consists of actual endpoints with finite energy. Continuous energy is E(u)=sum_{j=0}^n int u MA(u^[j],0^[n-j])/(n+1), with a continuous psh reference. O gives the genuine positive symmetric mixed Radon operator of raw mass V, affine in admissible curvature slots, independent of all decreasing continuous approximations. Every E1 test is integrable against every mixed output. On a common directed set, decreasing E1 slots and weights with E1 endpoints have joint weighted integral convergence. Actual E1 is convex, E is concave and decreasing-continuous, E(u+c)=E(u)+cV, and along u_t=(1-t)u+tv its energy is a polynomial of degree at most n+1 with derivative int(v-u) MA(u_t). Differences are used only on the common finite-value full-measure domain. Absolute energy class and operator are reference-independent; complete-field pushforward retains V. O's full continuous proof gives real PL density and representation f=h-k by FS metrics on one ample rational A; the continuous signed form D_Q(a,b)=-int a dd^c b Q is symmetric, positive semidefinite and satisfies Cauchy-Schwarz. Its smooth positivity uses boundaryless analytification and compact support from properness, not compactness alone. Its exact nonpositive integrability estimate is int(-w) MA(u_1,...,u_n)<=H_n[B(w)+sum B(u_r)], H_n=(n+1)^(n+1)/n!, B=-E, with nonpositive endpoints. The O clarification obtains this exact estimate by epsilon reference shifts when the original defining approximants are not nonpositive.

M states, at raw mass V, that all actual E1 scalars are absolutely mu-integrable iff the continuous dual J(mu)=sup_{continuous psh v}[E(v)-int v mu] is finite iff U_mu=sup_{sup u=0,B(u)<=1} int(-u) mu is finite. The continuous and all-E1 suprema agree. It constructs one selected original reference with moment int(-u) MA(0)<=M_0 for every sup-normalized actual psh u, before E1 membership. For finite U, d_n=n(n+1)/2, it gives F_mu(u)<=-B(u)+U(1+2M_0)+U sqrt(2d_n B(u)), hence J(mu)<=U(1+2M_0)+(d_n/2)U^2. For an already known genuine output MA(u)=mu, u attains this dual. These statements do not manufacture inverse existence. Its atomic/moment claims apply to the selected reference, not an arbitrary replacement reference, and finite U is a material target hypothesis.

D provides actual invariant singular descent and invariant Radon lifting after invariance is proved, not inverse existence. C grants strict locality/comparison, not every-point uniqueness. N's norming-atom hypothesis is conditional. T already settles the trivial-valued ample equation in all dimensions. Q/G settle their projective-line/genus-zero sectors. S269 already settles every original all-genus curve, raw degree mass, arbitrary intrinsic support, attained dual and every-solution every-point uniqueness modulo a finite constant. It does not settle general n>=2. These seven grants are fully registered/read but are not additional analytic premises of the new stability proof. Failed/private/working records are not grants.

Domains are projective continuous psh-regularizable rational-bundle metrics; geometric reducedness/semiampleness hold here. Real weight group R handles trivial valuations. notes.summary: New all-field n>=2 nonordered MA stability and exact Bregman/midpoint identities; c_n=(1-2^-n)/(2(n+1)). Zero defect is equivalent to equality of all successive mixed measures; fibres are convex. No every-point potential uniqueness.
notes.detailedSummary: Extends nonnegative Dirichlet coefficients from continuous stages using four O weighted integrals; proves PL-test bounds, exact supporting-plane coefficients (n-j)/(n+1), tent coefficients with their exact endpoint minimum, and all mixed-measure rigidity of each operator fibre. At a known solution, dual error quantitatively controls MA output error. No inverse is constructed and equality modulo finite constants is not inferred.
notes.text:
New proved draft theorem, relative to n1: nonordered finite-energy stability, exact energy-defect formulas, and equality of all mixed measures in each genuine operator fibre. Domain: every retained n>=2, original arbitrary complete real-valued field, smooth geometrically integral projective X and actual ample rational L; no support, invariance, product or skeleton restriction. All masses are V, and potentials are actual E1 endpoints.

Fix the reference and u,v in E1. In integrals set d=v-u on common finite-value full-measure sets. Put rho_j=MA(u^[n-j],v^[j]) for 0<=j<=n, D_j=int d(rho_j-rho_{j+1}) for 0<=j<n, and I=int d(MA(u)-MA(v))=sum D_j. All numbers are finite by O integrability. For any real PL test f=h-k on an ample rational A set C_f=2||f||_infinity(A.L^(n-1)). Then D_j>=0, |int f(rho_j-rho_{j+1})|^2<=C_f D_j, and |int f(MA(u)-MA(v))|^2<=n C_f I. There is no ordering assumption.

Proof: for continuous endpoints let Q_j=theta_u^(n-1-j)theta_v^j. The continuous signed form D_Q(a,b)=-int a dd^c b Q is symmetric and nonnegative by smooth Stokes/positivity, then uniform regularization and bounded total variation; positivity of its real quadratic polynomial gives Cauchy-Schwarz. D_j=D_Qj(d,d), and rho_j-rho_{j+1}=-dd^c d Q_j. The two positive measures dd^c h Q_j and dd^c k Q_j have mass (A.L^(n-1)), so 0<=D_Qj(f,f)<=C_f. Cauchy-Schwarz gives the individual test bound. For singular u,v choose independent continuous decreasing nets u_a,v_b on their product directed set. Each D_j is four integrals with weight u_a or v_b and slots from u_a,v_b. O's joint weighted law passes every integral separately; their nonnegative limits are the claimed D_j. Weak convergence passes the continuous f tests. The bound C_f is independent of the approximants, hence passes as well. No singular curvature product on A and no convergence of a nonmonotone difference is presumed. Telescoping and sum sqrt(D_j)<=sqrt(n sum D_j) give the pure bound.

For u_t=(1-t)u+tv and g(t)=E(u_t), the finite curvature polynomial and granted affine derivative give -g''(t)=n sum_{j=0}^{n-1} binom(n-1,j)t^j(1-t)^(n-1-j)D_j. Equivalently pass finite coefficients from continuous endpoints using the four weighted integrals above. Define B_u(v)=E(u)-E(v)+int(v-u)MA(u) and Delta=E((u+v)/2)-(E(u)+E(v))/2. Two integrations of g'' give B_u(v)=int_0^1(1-t)(-g'')dt and B_v(u)=int_0^1 t(-g'')dt. The integer beta integral, proved by repeated integration by parts, yields B_u(v)=sum [(n-j)/(n+1)]D_j and B_v(u)=sum [(j+1)/(n+1)]D_j. Consequently I/(n+1)<=B_u(v)<=n I/(n+1), and B_u(v)+B_v(u)=I.

The tent G(t)=min(t,1-t)/2 vanishes at the endpoints and has derivative jump -1 at 1/2. Piecewise integration by parts gives Delta=int_0^1 G(-g'')dt=sum alpha_{n,j}D_j, alpha_{n,j}=n binom(n-1,j) int_0^1 G(t)t^j(1-t)^(n-1-j)dt. Its exact minimum is c_n=(1-2^(-n))/(2(n+1)). To verify the minimum for every n, write b_{m,j}=binom(m,j)t^j(1-t)^(m-j). Symmetry gives alpha_j=alpha_{n-1-j}. Since b'_{n,j+1}=n(b_{n-1,j}-b_{n-1,j+1}), alpha_{j+1}-alpha_j=(int_0^(1/2)b_{n,j+1}-int_(1/2)^1 b_{n,j+1})/2. For j+1<=n/2, b(t)/b(1-t)=(t/(1-t))^(2(j+1)-n)>=1 on 0<t<=1/2, so the coefficients increase toward their middle, then decrease by symmetry. Their minimum is the endpoint. The polynomial g=-(1-t)^(n+1)/(n+1), with -g''=n(1-t)^(n-1), gives endpoint coefficient (1/2-2^(-(n+1)))/(n+1)=c_n. Thus Delta>=c_n I and |int f(MA(u)-MA(v))|^2<=(n C_f/c_n)Delta.

I=0 implies every nonnegative D_j=0. The individual test bound makes rho_j-rho_{j+1} vanish on every real PL scalar; uniform density and TV<=2V identify the signed Radon measures as zero. Conversely equal pure measures make the defining finite integral I zero. Positive alpha also gives Delta=0 iff I=0. Therefore zero I, zero midpoint deficit, equality of pure MA measures, and equality of all rho_j are equivalent. If two potentials have one pure measure, the curvature binomial expansion gives that same measure on their whole segment. Induction gives it on every convex combination of finitely many fibre elements. For w_1,...,w_n in the fibre, all nonempty subset averages w_S are in the fibre; O polarization gives MA(w_1,...,w_n)=sum_{S nonempty}(-1)^(n-|S|)|S|^n MA(w_S)/n!. Inclusion-exclusion counts n! maps onto n labels, so the scalar coefficients sum to one and the mixed measure equals the common pure measure. This proves convexity and all mixed-measure rigidity of each genuine fibre. It does not prove pointwise equality modulo constants.

If an actual solution u with MA(u)=mu is already known, n1's M theorem gives F_mu(u)=J(mu). Hence J(mu)-F_mu(v)=B_u(v), so I/(n+1)<=J-F_mu(v)<=n I/(n+1) and |int f(MA(v)-mu)|^2<=n(n+1)C_f[J-F_mu(v)]. All mixed outputs of actual solutions of the same target equal mu. This is quantitative stability at an existing genuine output, not inverse existence or every-point uniqueness. Every equality/inequality above is a mathematical argument from n1, not an inference from a finite grid.

The complete standalone proof is also in P16.4-argument.md and P16.4-paper.tex. Rerun exact coefficient diagnostics with python finite_checks.py and build with python build_deliverable.py. Program success and compilation are not mathematical acceptance.

notes.summary: Every intrinsic target has a common finite-energy weak limit of all genuine MA maximizing-net outputs, with an explicit PL error rate and mixed convergence. Does not identify the limit with the target or realize an actual maximizer; original remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Midpoint stability makes all maximizing nets measure-Cauchy; density/Riesz gives a canonical raw-mass-V limit. Material M finite-U coercivity plus O test integrability and lower-semicontinuous Radon passage show the limit itself satisfies the intrinsic condition. The limit is reference independent and equals the target when a genuine solution already exists. Gives exact competitor Euler inequalities and isolates actual attainment, target identification and every-point zero-I rigidity as unresolved sufficient steps.
notes.text:
New proved draft theorem, relative to n1 and n2: for every intrinsic target mu, every variational maximizing net has the same weak limit lambda_mu of its genuine MA outputs; this limit is itself an intrinsic finite-energy measure. This is not an inverse-defined Monge-Ampere operator, not an assertion lambda_mu=mu, and not realization by an actual potential. Retain the original n>=2 arbitrary-field/ample/projective smooth domain and raw mass V.

Define F_mu(u)=E(u)-int u mu and epsilon(u)=J(mu)-F_mu(u)>=0 on actual E1; n1 gives finite J and equality of continuous/all-E1 suprema. Concavity and cancellation of the affine integral term imply Delta(u,v)=F_mu((u+v)/2)-(F_mu(u)+F_mu(v))/2<=(epsilon(u)+epsilon(v))/2. Apply n2's midpoint estimate: |int f(MA(u)-MA(v))|^2<=n C_f(epsilon(u)+epsilon(v))/(2c_n) for each real PL test.

Choose continuous tests u_k with epsilon(u_k)<=1/k from the finite real supremum. This is an ordinary maximizing sequence, not a cofinal sequence for the carrier or FS nets. Their MA integrals are Cauchy on each PL test. For any continuous f choose PL p uniformly close; the error for two raw-mass-V measures is <=2V||f-p||. Thus the integrals are Cauchy on every continuous test. Their limits define a positive bounded linear functional on C(T) of value V at one. Compact Hausdorff Riesz representation gives a positive Radon lambda_mu of mass V. Compare any other maximizing net with that sequence using the same double-index estimate; its PL integrals have the same limits, and density/mass pass this to every continuous test. Therefore all maximizing nets converge to lambda_mu, independently of the net. Comparing a fixed u to the sequence also gives |int f(MA(u)-lambda_mu)|^2<=n C_f epsilon(u)/(2c_n).

To prove intrinsic energy of this limit, work in M's selected original reference. Normalize the maximizing sequence by finite constants, sup u_k=0, B=-E>=0. Let U=U_mu<infinity, d_n=n(n+1)/2, C=U(1+2M_0), a=U sqrt(2d_n), and R=((a+sqrt(a^2+4(C+1)))/2)^2. Since J>=F_mu(0)=0, a maximizing tail has F_mu(u_k)>=-1. M's material finite-U estimate F_mu(u_k)<=-B(u_k)+C+a sqrt(B(u_k)) implies B(u_k)<=R by the quadratic inequality. Moment alone is not used to obtain this bound.

For any actual normalized w in E1, O's exact all-test bound with n identical curvature slots is int(-w) MA(u_k)<=H_n[B(w)+nB(u_k)]<=H_n[B(w)+nR], H_n=(n+1)^(n+1)/n!. The function -w is nonnegative lower semicontinuous. For positive Radon measures on compact Hausdorff T, weak convergence implies int(-w)lambda_mu<=liminf int(-w)MA(u_k): express this integral as the supremum of continuous nonnegative minorant integrals, using inner compact approximation at finitely many open superlevels and normality, and pass each minorant through weak convergence. Thus int(-w)lambda_mu<=H_n[B(w)+nR]<infinity. Finite constant shifts recover absolute integrability of every unnormalized actual E1 scalar. Raw mass is V, so M applies to lambda_mu and gives finite J(lambda_mu). Explicitly U_lambda<=H_n(1+nR) and J(lambda_mu)<=U_lambda(1+2M_0)+(d_n/2)U_lambda^2. This reference-dependent estimate is stated only in M's selected reference, without transferring its atoms to a new reference.

For mixed convergence take n slots from any finitely many maximizing nets on their product directed set. Each nonempty subset average is actual E1 and has error <=the average of its slots' errors by concavity, hence is another maximizing net. Each corresponding pure output tends to lambda_mu. O's finite polarization formula and its coefficient sum one give convergence of the full genuine mixed output to lambda_mu. If an actual maximizer exists, its constant net shows its pure output equals lambda_mu. Every mixed output of actual maximizers also equals lambda_mu by n2. If an actual genuine solution exists, M makes it a maximizer and its constant output is mu; consequently lambda_mu=mu in that conditional case.

Reference independence follows without a new moment premise. If psi'=psi+b is continuous psh, scalars correspond u'=u-b and O gives E_psi'(u')=E_psi(u)-E_psi(b). F_psi',mu(u')=F_psi,mu(u)-E_psi(b)+int b mu; the same finite correction changes J, leaving epsilon unchanged. Absolute outputs are unchanged. The limit of the corresponding maximizing nets is therefore the same lambda_mu.

There is an exact competitor-direction Euler condition: an actual u maximizes F_mu iff int(v-u)[MA(u)-mu]<=0 for every actual v in E1. Every integral is finite by O and intrinsic integrability. Necessity is the one-sided derivative at t=0 of F_mu((1-t)u+tv). Sufficiency follows from the concave supporting inequality F_mu(v)-F_mu(u)<=that derivative, and equality of the all-E1 supremum with J. These inequalities do not give both signs of a general continuous perturbation, so PL density does not turn them into equality of the two measures.

Three sufficient missing steps for the original equation by this route are: (1) actual attainment F_mu(u)=J for every intrinsic target, rather than only measure convergence or abstract potential limits; (2) lambda_mu=mu for every such target, or complete actual-envelope/orthogonality/both-sign differentiation replacements proving the equation; (3) I(u,v)=0 implies u=v+c at every analytic point for one finite constant. n2 proves equality of all mixed measures at zero I, not pointwise determination, including common poles. If (1) and (2) were proved, the constant maximizing net would give the genuine equation; if (3) were also proved it would give every-solution every-point uniqueness. None of these three antecedents is established here. Finite-U coercivity, C comparison and D descent do not supply them. Curves are already S269 and not a new higher-dimensional inverse. The full remaining original P16.4 stays open, candidate=false.
